text:
maria: quick UX pass on the routing editor prototype. two things stood out: long rule titles are forced into one line and get truncated, and the preview now has a playback scrubber that auto-plays results 1 which can be noisy. screenshot + gif: https://mock.redwood/dev/routing-scrubber.gif

jon: truncation is rough. can we allow wrapping to two lines with ellipsis only after that? preserves more context without massive layout changes.

ashley: agree on 2-line wrap. but need to cap card height. also propose showing full name on hover and in the inspector panel.

kevin: a11y: wrapping is fine, but ensure focus ring doesn't shift layout. for the scrubber: auto-play should be off by default. if we keep auto-play, announce start/stop via `aria-live=polite` and provide a clear "Pause" control reachable by keyboard.

sam: scrubber UX thought: when preview runs show a timeline of routing events, users want to jump to the failing step. add step markers and a "Jump to failure" button that anchors the canvas to the rule in question.

olivia: love the jump-to-failure idea. for long simulations, we should compress the timeline into clusters and let users zoom in. keeps overview manageable.

maria: good. also a copy/label tweak: scrubber control currently reads "Playback" in the mock. change to "Simulation playback" and make tooltips explicit: "Play/pause routing simulation; use scrubber to inspect token-by-token routing."

jon: keyboard shortcut idea: allow `Ctrl+ArrowUp/Down` to move a focused rule. Add a visible hint in the card tooltip so power users discover it. But also include accessible move buttons for non-modifier users.

kevin: confirm modifier shortcuts don't conflict with browser or OS keys. include ability to remap or disable in preferences. and ensure screen readers announce reorders: "Rule X moved to position 3" using `aria-live="assertive"` for reorder actions.

sam: validation flows: when a rule fails only in simulation (vs config time) we currently badge it same as a config error. separate states: "config error" vs "simulation mismatch" with different colors and explanatory tooltip/copy. avoids alarm fatigue.

ashley: agree. visual language: use amber/orange for simulation mismatches, red for config validation. also ensure tokens meet contrast (we're using orange-600 now, double-check for 12px labels).

maria: implementation notes: ashley will mock two-line wrapping + compressed timeline; jon will prototype keyboard hint and context menu move items; kevin will write the aria announcement spec (reorder + playback start/stop + failure jump); sam will enumerate simulation mismatch UX states and sample copy; olivia will sketch timeline clustering interactions. i'll update the prototype and post a short screencap.

design-bot: Created task: "POLICY-PLAYBACK: scrubber accessibility + failure-jump + rule wrapping" (EPIC-3727).

jon: small perf nit: when many rules exist the timeline events are expensive to render. virtualize markers and lazy-load details on hover.

kevin: also add to QA: voiceover test for reorder announcements, NVDA check for scrubber controls, keyboard-only navigation of timeline clusters.

ashley: accessibility poke: when a card expands to show wrapped title, ensure it doesn't push other elements off-screen unexpectedly. prefer overlay tooltip for the full title if expansion would cause layout shift.

maria: let's prefer 2-line wrap + tooltip overlay on overflow. that feels safer. i'll update the mock and attach the new GIF later today. closing thread until then.

sam: i'll wire the mismatch states into the preview harness so we can run a11y + regressions once the mock is up.

kevin: ping me after the new gif, i'll run a focused accessibility pass.

olivia: thanks team. excited for the failure-jump UX.

maria: thanks everyone.
